thread:
jamie: Hey infra team — noticing duplicate Atlantis 'plan' runs for prod-services in redwood/inference. It looks like the GitHub Actions workflow is firing twice (PR + push) when contributors push to a branch in-repo. Anyone seen this pattern and best fix? :confused:

alex: Yup, seen that. Common when the PR is from a branch in the same repo — both push and pull_request events can fire for the same commit. Quick questions: is the workflow configured to run plan on both push and pull_request, or is Atlantis being triggered twice via a webhook + GHA?

jamie: Here's the workflow header we have (simplified):
```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    types: [ opened, synchronize, reopened ]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        region: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run atlantis plan
        uses: runatlantis/atlantis-gha@v1
```

alex: OK. Two pragmatic fixes (pick one):
- Make plan job conditional so it only runs for pull_request events: `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` 
- Or add a concurrency group that collapses duplicate runs for the same PR/sha: 
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
Either avoids double execution. Also consider restricting triggers with `paths` so only infra folder changes run plan.

sasha: Also watch out for `pull_request_target` — it runs in the base branch context and will have secrets, but is a security risk for untrusted forks. If you depend on secrets for the Atlantis step, avoid `pull_request_target` unless you validate the PR.

jamie: Good call. We do run matrix across regions which multiplies the runs. If we add concurrency group, will that cancel in-flight runs or let them queue?

alex: With `cancel-in-progress: false` they won't be canceled but the group prevents parallel runs for the same key. If you want to cancel old runs, set it to `true`. For our use case I'd set false and rely on `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` plus `paths` to be explicit.

jamie: One other problem surfaced: after a recent deploy ArgoCD apps lost a SecretRef (kustomize overlay didn't preserve `secretGenerator` name). Example ArgoCD Application manifest had `envFrom: secretRef: { name: null }` after kustomize build. Any tips?

sasha: That rings a bell — kustomize `secretGenerator` can produce names with hashes unless you set `options: disableNameSuffixHash: true`. Alternatively, annotate the ArgoCD Application to point at an existing secret using `spec.source.kustomize.forceCommonLabels: true`? (note: mixing approaches can be brittle).

alex: Another pattern we've used: bake the secret as part of the cluster (secret created out-of-band) and reference it in the Application via `spec.source.plugin` or use `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-ref: <name>` annotation depending on your ArgoCD operator. But if you want kustomize-created secrets, set `disableNameSuffixHash: true` in the kustomization.yaml so the name is stable.

jamie: Thanks. I'll try: (1) remove the `push` trigger for the plan job (leave push for apply only), (2) add `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` to plan, and (3) add `paths` to only run for `infra/**`. Also will set `disableNameSuffixHash: true` on the kustomize overlay for argocd secrets.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new commit pushed to infra/ci-config (sha: ab12c3d) — CI started :rocket:

jamie: Implemented change and pushed `infra/ci-config`@ab12c3d — removed push trigger from plan job and added path filter. Running smoke tests now.

alex: Nice — if you want I can watch for duplicated Atlantis plans over next 24h and revert if we see regressions. :eyes:

jamie: Appreciate it, thanks all. Will follow up if any fallout. :thumbsup:
